items.stem: What is the name for "a long, hollow tube made of dead cells joined end to end with no end walls, with lignified walls, that carries water and mineral ions"?
items.answer: Xylem vessel
items.markingKey: Xylem vessel: a long, hollow tube made of dead cells joined end to end with no end walls, with lignified walls, that carries water and mineral ions.

items.stem: Compare the structure of xylem vessels and phloem sieve tubes.
items.answer: Xylem: dead, lignified, no end walls, no cytoplasm, pits. Phloem: living, cellulose walls, sieve plates, little cytoplasm, no nucleus, companion cells. Both: long tubes of cells joined end to end.
items.markingKey: two differences [2]; one similarity [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain why the xylem in a root is in the centre.
items.answer: Central position resists the pulling (tension) forces as the plant is anchored, and receives water passing through the endodermis.
items.markingKey: Central position resists the pulling (tension) forces as the plant is anchored [1]; and receives water passing through the endodermis [1] [2]

items.stem: A micrograph of a root hair has a scale bar labelled 200 μm. The scale bar is 20 mm long and the image of a root hair is 120 mm long. (a) Use the scale bar to calculate the magnification. (b) Calculate the actual length of a root hair.

A micrograph of a vascular bundle has a scale bar labelled 200 μm. The scale bar is 20 mm long and the image of a vascular bundle is 34 mm long. (a) Use the scale bar to calculate the magnification. (b) Calculate the actual length of a vascular bundle.

Ravi examined a transverse section of a privet (Ligustrum) leaf with a light microscope and made a low-power plan diagram. (a) Describe the distribution of xylem and phloem in this organ. (b) Explain how the stain toluidine blue or phloroglucinol helps to identify xylem.
items.answer: (a) Stem: vascular bundles in a ring, xylem inside, phloem outside. Root: central xylem (star / X shape) with phloem between the arms. Leaf: xylem upper, phloem lower in the midrib. (b) Lignin stains differently (red with phloroglucinol / blue-green with toluidine blue), so lignified xylem is distinguished.
items.markingKey: (a) any 2 from: Stem: vascular bundles in a ring, xylem inside, phloem outside; Root: central xylem (star / X shape) with phloem between the arms; Leaf: xylem upper, phloem lower in the midrib (1 mark each) [2] (b) Lignin stains differently (red with phloroglucinol / blue-green with toluidine blue) [1]; so lignified xylem is distinguished [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain the role of lignin in xylem.
items.answer: Strengthens walls so vessels do not collapse under tension; waterproof; supports the plant.
items.markingKey: any 2 from: Strengthens walls so vessels do not collapse under tension; waterproof; supports the plant (1 mark each) [2]

items.stem: Lina says: "Phloem carries water up the plant and xylem carries sugar down." Explain whether Lina is correct.
items.answer: Xylem carries water and minerals upwards; phloem carries assimilates (mainly sucrose) up and down.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Xylem carries water and minerals upwards; phloem carries assimilates (mainly sucrose) up and down. [2]

items.answer: Xylem: dead, lignified, no end walls, pits; continuous column, resists tension. Sieve tubes: living, sieve plates, few organelles, mass flow. Companion cells: nucleus, many mitochondria and ribosomes, plasmodesmata, active loading.

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "apoplast pathway"?
options: A band of suberin in the walls of endodermal cells that blocks the apoplast pathway.
The movement of water through the cytoplasm of cells, connected by plasmodesmata.
The movement of water through cell walls and intercellular spaces.
The attraction between water molecules due to hydrogen bonds, allowing a continuous column of water to be pulled up xylem.
items.answer: The movement of water through cell walls and intercellular spaces.
items.markingKey: Apoplast pathway: the movement of water through cell walls and intercellular spaces.

items.stem: Explain how water moves from the soil into the xylem of a root.
items.answer: Water enters root hair cells by osmosis (higher ψ in soil); moves across cortex via apoplast (cell walls) and symplast (cytoplasm, plasmodesmata); Casparian strip blocks apoplast at endodermis so water enters cytoplasm; enters xylem down a ψ gradient.
items.markingKey: Water enters root hair cells by osmosis (higher ψ in soil) [1]; moves across cortex via apoplast (cell walls) and symplast (cytoplasm, plasmodesmata) [1]; Casparian strip blocks apoplast at endodermis so water enters cytoplasm [1]; enters xylem down a ψ gradient [1] [4]

items.stem: Explain how the cohesion–tension theory accounts for the movement of water up the xylem.
items.answer: Water evaporates from mesophyll walls and diffuses out of stomata; water is drawn from xylem, creating tension; hydrogen bonds (cohesion) hold the column together and adhesion to lignified walls; the whole column is pulled up.
items.markingKey: Water evaporates from mesophyll walls and diffuses out of stomata [1]; water is drawn from xylem, creating tension [1]; hydrogen bonds (cohesion) hold the column together and adhesion to lignified walls [1]; the whole column is pulled up [1] [4]

items.stem: Arjun set up a bubble potometer with a leafy shoot and measured the distance moved by an air bubble along a capillary tube (radius 0.5 mm) in 5 minutes at different wind speeds produced by a fan. State the type of graph you would draw to display these results and what you would plot on each axis.
items.answer: A line graph: distance from fan on the x-axis and mean distance moved by bubble in 5 min on the y-axis.
items.markingKey: line graph (continuous independent variable) [1]; distance from fan on x-axis and distance moved by bubble in 5 min on y-axis [1] [2]

items.stem: Ethan set up a bubble potometer with a leafy shoot and measured the distance moved by an air bubble along a capillary tube (radius 0.5 mm) in 5 minutes at different wind speeds produced by a fan. (a) Describe the trend shown by the results. (b) Suggest one way to improve this investigation.
items.answer: (a) As the distance from fan increases, the distance moved by bubble in 5 min decreases and then levels off at about 80 cm. (b) Leave the shoot to acclimatise for 5 minutes at each distance.

items.stem: Explain why the rate of transpiration increases with temperature.
items.answer: Water molecules gain kinetic energy, so evaporation from cell walls and diffusion of water vapour out of stomata increase; warmer air holds more water vapour, increasing the ψ gradient.

items.answer: (a) Water moves through cytoplasm of cells, from cell to cell via plasmodesmata, by osmosis. (b) Tension in xylem during high transpiration pulls vessel walls inwards slightly.

items.stem: A plant physiologist in Kathmandu supplied a dye that moves only through cell walls to the roots of a eucalyptus tree 60 m tall. The dye was found in the walls of cortex cells but stopped at the endodermis. (a) Name the pathway taken by the dye and explain why it stopped at the endodermis. (b) Explain the advantage to the plant of the Casparian strip.
items.answer: (a) Apoplast pathway; the Casparian strip (suberin) in endodermal walls blocks movement through cell walls. (b) Water and ions must pass through cell surface membranes / cytoplasm, so the plant controls which ions enter xylem; prevents back-flow; allows root pressure.

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "succulent"?
options: The number of stomata per unit area of leaf surface.
A xerophytic dune grass with rolled leaves, sunken stomata and hairs.
A plant that stores water in swollen leaves or stems.
A plant adapted to survive in dry conditions with little available water.
items.answer: A plant that stores water in swollen leaves or stems.

items.stem: Explain how rolled leaves and hairs reduce water loss in marram grass.
items.answer: They trap moist air close to the stomata, raising the water potential outside the stomata, reducing the water potential gradient, so less water vapour diffuses out.

items.stem: Under the same conditions, a mesophyte lost 9 g of water per day and marram grass on a sand dune of similar leaf area lost 2 g per day. (a) Describe three structural adaptations that could explain the difference. (b) Suggest a disadvantage of these adaptations for the plant.

items.stem: Explain how CAM plants such as cacti reduce water loss but still photosynthesise.

items.stem: Explain how sucrose is loaded into phloem sieve tubes.
items.answer: Proton pumps in companion cell membranes use ATP to pump H⁺ out; H⁺ diffuses back in with sucrose through co-transporter proteins; sucrose passes into sieve tube via plasmodesmata (or directly).

items.stem: Explain how mass flow moves sap from source to sink.
items.answer: At the source sucrose is loaded, lowering ψ; water enters from xylem by osmosis, raising hydrostatic pressure; at the sink sucrose is removed, water leaves; sap flows down the pressure gradient from source to sink.
items.markingKey: At the source sucrose is loaded, lowering ψ [1]; water enters from xylem by osmosis, raising hydrostatic pressure [1]; at the sink sucrose is removed, water leaves [1]; sap flows down the pressure gradient from source to sink [1] [4]

Ethan examined a transverse section of a buttercup (Ranunculus) root with a light microscope and made a low-power plan diagram. (a) Explain how the stain toluidine blue or phloroglucinol helps to identify xylem. (b) Describe how the structure of a companion cell is related to its function.
items.answer: (a) Lignin stains differently (red with phloroglucinol / blue-green with toluidine blue), so lignified xylem is distinguished. (b) Many mitochondria (ATP for active loading), many ribosomes, nucleus controls sieve element, plasmodesmata link to sieve element.
items.markingKey: (a) Lignin stains differently (red with phloroglucinol / blue-green with toluidine blue) [1]; so lignified xylem is distinguished [1] [2] (b) any 3 from: Many mitochondria (ATP for active loading); many ribosomes; nucleus controls sieve element; plasmodesmata link to sieve element (1 mark each) [3]

items.stem: Why does the Casparian strip force water into the symplast pathway?
options: It is waterproof suberin in the endodermal cell walls
It is made of lignified xylem
items.answer: It is waterproof suberin in the endodermal cell walls
items.markingKey: Water must cross cell surface membranes, allowing control of ions.

items.stem: Explain why a shoot must be cut and fitted to a potometer under water.
items.answer: To prevent air entering the xylem, which would break the continuous water column (air lock).
items.markingKey: To prevent air entering the xylem [1]; which would break the continuous water column (air lock) [1] [2]

items.stem: A student in Mumbai states: "Water is actively pumped up the xylem using ATP." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: Water moves passively by cohesion–tension; xylem vessels are dead.

items.stem: A bubble in the capillary tube of a potometer (internal radius 0.75 mm) moved 54 mm in 5 minutes. (a) Calculate the volume of water taken up. (b) Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.
items.answer: (a) 95.4 mm³ (b) 19.09 mm³ min⁻¹

items.stem: Jonas set up a bubble potometer with a leafy shoot and measured the distance moved by an air bubble along a capillary tube (radius 0.5 mm) in 5 minutes at different wind speeds produced by a fan. Results table. Distance from fan / cm: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. Distance moved by bubble in 5 min / mm, trial 1: 37, 29, 25, 22, 21; trial 2: 40, 18, 25, 22, 21; trial 3: 38, 30, 25, 22, 21. Calculate the mean distance moved by bubble in 5 min at 40 cm, ignoring any anomalous result.

A plant physiologist in Doha supplied a dye that moves only through cell walls to the roots of a mangrove tree. The dye was found in the walls of cortex cells but stopped at the endodermis. (a) Explain the advantage to the plant of the Casparian strip. (b) Suggest why the diameter of the trunk of a tree decreases slightly during the day.
items.answer: (a) Water and ions must pass through cell surface membranes / cytoplasm, so the plant controls which ions enter xylem; prevents back-flow; allows root pressure. (b) Tension in xylem during high transpiration pulls vessel walls inwards slightly.
items.markingKey: (a) any 2 from: Water and ions must pass through cell surface membranes / cytoplasm, so the plant controls which ions enter xylem; prevents back-flow; allows root pressure (1 mark each) [2] (b) Tension in xylem during high transpiration pulls vessel walls inwards slightly [2] [2]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "hydrophyte"?
options: A plant that stores water in swollen leaves or stems.
The number of stomata per unit area of leaf surface.
A plant adapted to survive in dry conditions with little available water.
A plant adapted to live in water.
items.answer: A plant adapted to live in water.
items.markingKey: Hydrophyte: a plant adapted to live in water.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain why xerophytes cannot simply close all stomata permanently. (b) Explain how rolled leaves and hairs reduce water loss in marram grass.
items.answer: (a) Stomata are needed for gas exchange: CO₂ must enter for photosynthesis. (b) They trap moist air close to the stomata, raising the water potential outside the stomata, reducing the water potential gradient, so less water vapour diffuses out.
items.markingKey: (a) Stomata are needed for gas exchange: CO₂ must enter for photosynthesis [2] [2] (b) any 3 from: They trap moist air close to the stomata; raising the water potential outside the stomata; reducing the water potential gradient; so less water vapour diffuses out (1 mark each) [3]

items.stem: Kenji made a nail-varnish impression of the lower epidermis of a bean leaf and counted stomata in five fields of view, each 0.5 mm in diameter: 17, 17, 22, 17, 23. (a) Calculate the mean number of stomata per field of view. (b) Calculate the stomatal density in stomata per mm².

Samuel made a nail-varnish impression of the lower epidermis of a maize leaf and counted stomata in five fields of view, each 0.4 mm in diameter: 22, 24, 19, 25, 22. (a) Calculate the mean number of stomata per field of view. (b) Calculate the stomatal density in stomata per mm². (c) Explain why several fields of view were counted.
items.answer: (a) 22.4 (b) 178 mm⁻² (c) Stomata are not evenly distributed; a mean of several areas is more representative.
items.markingKey: (a) 112 ÷ 5 = 22.4 [1] (b) area = π × 0.2² = 0.126 mm² [1]; 22.4 ÷ 0.126 = 178 mm⁻² [1] (c) uneven distribution / representative [1] [4]

items.stem: Under the same conditions, a mesophyte lost 10 g of water per day and marram grass on a sand dune of similar leaf area lost 3 g per day. (a) Describe three structural adaptations that could explain the difference. (b) Describe how you could compare the water loss of the two plants in a laboratory.
items.answer: (a) Thick cuticle; sunken stomata; rolled leaves; hairs; fewer stomata; small leaves / spines. (b) Weigh potted plants (pots sealed in plastic) at intervals, or use a potometer; same conditions; calculate loss per unit leaf area.
items.markingKey: (a) any 3 from: Thick cuticle; sunken stomata; rolled leaves; hairs; fewer stomata; small leaves / spines (1 mark each) [3] (b) Weigh potted plants (pots sealed in plastic) at intervals, or use a potometer [1]; same conditions [1]; calculate loss per unit leaf area [1] [3]

items.stem: A student in Lisbon states: "Phloem only carries sugars downwards to the roots." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: Phloem transports assimilates from source to sink in either direction.

items.stem: Sofia says: "Sucrose moves through phloem by diffusion." Explain whether Sofia is correct.
items.answer: Sap moves by mass flow down a hydrostatic pressure gradient.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Sap moves by mass flow down a hydrostatic pressure gradient. [2]

items.stem: A leaf of a sugar beet plant was supplied with ¹⁴CO₂. Radioactive sucrose was detected in an aphid stylet 80 cm below the leaf after 90 minutes. (a) Calculate the rate of translocation in mm min⁻¹. (b) Explain how the ¹⁴C came to be in sucrose in the phloem. (c) Explain why aphid stylets are useful in investigating translocation.
items.answer: (a) 8.89 mm min⁻¹ (b) ¹⁴CO₂ was fixed in photosynthesis into sugars, converted to sucrose and loaded into phloem at the source. (c) The stylet penetrates a single sieve tube, so pure phloem sap can be collected and analysed (and pressure shown by sap exuding).
items.markingKey: (a) 800 mm ÷ 90 min = 8.89 [2] (b) photosynthesis [1]; loaded into phloem [1] (c) single sieve tube / pure sap [1] [5]

items.stem: Explain how assimilates are transported from sources to sinks in a plant.
items.answer: Sources and sinks defined with examples; sucrose made in mesophyll; proton pumps and co-transporters load companion cells and sieve tubes (ATP); low ψ, water enters by osmosis from xylem; high hydrostatic pressure; mass flow; unloading at sinks (diffusion / active), converted to starch or used; water returns to xylem.
items.markingKey: source / sink [1]; loading mechanism [2]; osmosis and pressure [2]; mass flow and unloading [2] [7]

items.stem: Why do xylem vessels have no end walls?
options: So that water can flow in a continuous column with little resistance
items.answer: So that water can flow in a continuous column with little resistance
items.markingKey: Dead, hollow, no cross-walls.

items.stem: Tariq says: "Sieve tube elements are dead cells like xylem vessels." Explain whether Tariq is correct.
items.answer: Sieve tube elements are living but have no nucleus; they depend on companion cells.

items.stem: Describe and explain the structural and physiological adaptations of xerophytic plants that reduce water loss.

items.stem: A farmer in Singapore removed a ring of bark (including the phloem) from the trunk of a mango tree. After some weeks, the bark above the ring swelled and the roots began to die, but the leaves did not wilt. (a) Explain why the roots eventually died. (b) Explain why the leaves did not wilt. (c) Describe the mass flow hypothesis for translocation.
items.answer: (a) Roots are sinks; no sucrose reached them for respiration, so no ATP for active uptake / growth. (b) Xylem (inside the phloem, in the wood) was intact, so water continued to move up. (c) Loading at source lowers ψ; water enters; high hydrostatic pressure; unloading at sink; flow down pressure gradient.
